task.description: Rework 1 of 3 for ISS-0427 design, per CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's Step 2b FAIL (relayed by the coordinator; the validator's own handoff file at handoffs/WF03-ISS0427-20260904/step-02b-code-design-validator.json does not exist on disk despite being referenced -- worked from the coordinator's inline relay, which was detailed and self-contained). Two findings to fix: (1) BLOCKER -- section 3.2 dimension 3's pg_constraint contype enumeration claimed {c,f,p,u} was the full set Postgres defines, which is false (x=exclusion, t=constraint trigger also exist); (2) MAJOR -- table-level storage parameters (pg_class.reloptions) were silently uncovered by the parity check, unlike triggers/comments/collations/privileges which were each explicitly ruled out. Also required: run a systematic catalog walk (not just patch the two holes) asking what else a degraded clone could differ in that the check wouldn't see, and add the sentence stating the reaper structurally cannot drop the template.

result.summary:
lib/letflow/design/iss0427-tenant-test-schema-template-clone.md updated in place. New section 0.2 documents a systematic, empirically-verified catalog walk across pg_class, pg_constraint, pg_attribute, pg_trigger, pg_statistic_ext, and information_schema.columns -- the six catalogs most likely to carry a table-shape property LIKE INCLUDING ALL could mishandle. Method: built throwaway probe_tpl/probe_clone schemas in letflow_dev deliberately provisioning every catalog-visible property this design's reasoning could plausibly miss (exclusion constraint, WITH (fillfactor=...) storage option, per-column SET STATISTICS, GENERATED ... STORED column, CREATE STATISTICS extended-stats object, a real CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER, table/column comments), cloned via LIKE INCLUDING ALL, compared both sides directly. All probe schemas dropped and verified gone via \dn before this handoff was written.

POINT 3 FINDINGS (the systematic walk, what I found beyond the two the validator flagged):

1. CORRECTED, not just supplemented: contype enumeration now lists all six kinds (c,f,p,u,x,t). Verified x (exclusion constraints) ARE actually copied correctly by LIKE INCLUDING ALL (index-backed, same mechanism as unique indexes) -- confirmed on two independent probes including a minimal isolation case. So the MECHANISM needed no fix for exclusion constraints; only the CHECK was blind to them. Folded into the existing per-table multiset constraint-definition comparison, no new step needed.

2. reloptions (validator's own MAJOR finding): reproduced exactly -- WITH (fillfactor=70, autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor=0.05) on template clones to empty reloptions. New dimension 9. Clarified precisely why: INCLUDING STORAGE copies per-column attstorage (plain/external/extended/main), a DIFFERENT 'storage' concept from table-level reloptions -- the prior draft conflated the two by name similarity. Currently a zero-vs-zero rule-out (grepped priv/repo/migrations/ for :options and WITH (, no hits in any tenant-scoped migration) -- not evidence of live divergence today, but now actively checked.

3. NEW GAP, found by this rework's own pass, not flagged by the validator: pg_attribute.attstattarget (per-column ALTER ... SET STATISTICS) is NOT copied by LIKE INCLUDING ALL -- verified directly, 500 on template becomes -1 (default sentinel) on clone. Same severity/shape class as reloptions. New dimension 10. Also currently zero-vs-zero (grepped, no SET STATISTICS in any migration).

4. NEW COVERAGE GAP in the opposite direction: pg_statistic_ext (CREATE STATISTICS extended-statistics objects) ARE copied by LIKE INCLUDING ALL, with an auto-renamed identifier (same renaming behavior already documented for indexes) -- verified directly (events_stat became events3_parent_id_total_stored_stat on a clone sibling). Correctly copied by the mechanism; the check simply never looked. New dimension 11, given the same name-independent structural-comparison treatment as indexes for when one is eventually added (none exist today, grepped, no hits).

5. Row security, partitioning, tablespace, ownership: explicitly checked via pg_class.relrowsecurity/relforcerowsecurity/relkind/relispartition/reltablespace/relowner on both sides -- all identical, all at defaults, consistent with grepping every migration for ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY / PARTITION BY / TABLESPACE (no hits). New dimension 12, an explicit rule-out matching the rigor already applied to triggers/comments/collations/privileges, not a silent gap.

6. Generated columns (GENERATED ALWAYS ... STORED, attgenerated='s') behave correctly under LIKE INCLUDING ALL and were already covered by the existing column-comparison dimension (generation expression is catalogued as a form of column default) -- recorded as 'considered, found already covered,' not a new dimension.

7. Constraint triggers (contype='t'): confirmed real via CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER (contrary to this design's own PRIOR WRONG CLAIM that 'Postgres constraint triggers aren't created via plain CREATE TRIGGER' -- that sentence is deleted and replaced with a REWORK NOTE stating the correction plainly, per the instruction not to bury it). Confirmed NOT copied by LIKE INCLUDING ALL (0 pg_trigger rows on a clone sibling). Folded into the existing triggers dimension (item 8's triggers sub-bullet), which now explicitly covers both plain and constraint triggers via the same pg_trigger query plus the contype='t' pg_constraint count -- not a separate dimension, since it is genuinely the same underlying property (a trigger-backed constraint is still a trigger).

No further gap found across the six catalogs walked. pg_policy was checked implicitly (relrowsecurity false everywhere means no policy can be in effect regardless of pg_policy contents). Sequences/ownership and indexes, already covered and re-confirmed correct by the validator, were not re-probed.

PARITY CHECK NOW HAS 12 DIMENSIONS (grown from 8) -- section 3.2's intro sentence and both section 3.4 use-site references updated to reflect the new count and dimension numbers (build-time self-check: #1-6 and #8-#12, excluding #7 for the stated reason; permanent regression test: all #1-12).

POINT 4 (reaper cannot drop the template): added to INV-4, and verified by READING test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex directly rather than asserting from memory -- sweep_orphans/2 selects candidates via 'SELECT id, tenant_id, schema_name FROM tenant_schemas WHERE provisioned_at < $1', the same tenant_schemas table Registration/list_registrations/0 reads, never pg_namespace directly. Since INV-4 guarantees no tenant_schemas row is ever inserted for "tenant_template", the reaper's own query can never return it -- stated as a free consequence of INV-4 holding, with the exact query quoted so a future reader does not have to re-derive it.

Everything the validator confirmed as already correct (FK textual rewrite across adversarial shapes, sequence recreation end-to-end, index-rename finding and structural comparison, template-name collision safety, scope discipline, OQ-1, the honest speedup claim) was left untouched -- not re-litigated, per the coordinator's explicit instruction.

No implementation code added -- verified by grep for elixir/ex fenced code blocks (none found) after all edits. No lib/ or test/ file touched by this rework, only the design doc.
